newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait, Iran to discuss boosting OPEC's price role.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait, Iran to discuss boosting OPEC's price role.

text.p: Oil ministers from Kuwait and Iran will discuss means of boosting the role of OPEC in stabilising oil prices, the Kuwaiti minister said on Saturday.

"During official talks we will tackle...mutual cooperation including coordination to give a bigger role to OPEC in preserving current (oil) prices," Isa al-Mazeedi told reporters at the arrival of his Iranian counterpart Gholamreza Aghazadeh.
"Iran and Kuwait are effective members at OPEC...(OPEC's June) meeting necessitates that we should have talks," Aghazadeh said through an Arabic-language interpreter.
"Adhering to OPEC resolutions, (preserving oil) prices and boosting these prices are among the common points between the two countries," he said.

Aghazadeh, on his first visit to fellow OPEC member Kuwait since shortly after the 1991 Gulf War, is due to deliver a message during his two-day visit to Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
Talks will also tackle settling the offshore border, said Aghazadeh. "With relief I would like to say there are no differnces or problems between us and Kuwait."
Experts say the offshore area shared between Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iran contains at least six billion barrls of oil.

Non-Arab Iran has a coastline along the entire Gulf waterway which it shares with Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and the Arab island state of Bahrain. Iraq, at the northwestern tip of the Gulf, also has access.
Kuwait has started talks with ally Saudi Arabia to settle the mutual offshore border paving the way for a bilateral agreement with Tehran on territorial waters.
Such border agreements would lay the territorial and legal framework for offshore oil exploration.
